cards.claim: The velocity of object 1 relative to object 2 is v12 = v1 - v2, where v1 and v2 are measured in a common reference frame.
cards.quote: Take care to distinguish it from velocity of object 1 relative to velocity of object 2 : v12= v1 − v2. Here v1 and v2 are velocities with reference to some common reference frame.

cards.claim: Velocity addition between frames: the velocity of P relative to S equals its velocity relative to S' plus the velocity of S' relative to S.
cards.quote: The velocity of a particle relative to S is equal to its velocity relative to S ′ S ′ plus the velocity of S ′ S ′ relative to S .

locator.section: 4.5 Relative Motion in One and Two Dimensions

cards.claim: Observers moving at constant velocity relative to each other measure the same acceleration for a particle.
cards.quote: This says the acceleration of a particle is the same as measured by two observers moving at a constant velocity relative to each other.

locator.section: 4.5 Relative Motion in One and Two Dimensions

cards.claim: The equal-acceleration result needs the velocity of S' relative to S to be constant (a_S'S = 0); if one frame accelerates relative to the other, the measured accelerations differ.
cards.quote: We see that if the velocity of S ′ S ′ relative to S is a constant, then a → S ′ S = 0 a → S ′ S = 0 and a → P S = a → P S ′ .

locator.section: 4.5 Relative Motion in One and Two Dimensions

cards.claim: This velocity-addition method is an approximation that breaks down near the speed of light (special relativity is needed there) but is very accurate at everyday speeds.
cards.quote: This method makes an approximation that breaks down near the speed of light, where the more accurate methods or special relativity are needed, but is extremely accurate for everyday speeds

cards.claim: Learners confuse the resultant of two velocities acting on one object (v1 + v2) with the relative velocity of one object with respect to another (v1 - v2).
cards.quote: An object subjected to two velocities v1 and v2 has a resultant velocity v = v1 + v2. Take care to distinguish it from velocity of object 1 relative to velocity of object 2
